problem: Find the area of the finite region bounded between the curve $x=2{y}^{2}-2$ and the $y$-axis.

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the $y$-intercepts of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8}{y}^{2}-6 & =0 \\ \frac{3}{8}{y}^{2} & =6 \\ {y}^{2} & =16 \\ y & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we draw a sketch of the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013903/assets/c5cd702bed84fd0ffc7f0e3a9510bdb3411bb8f77424786f9445c4d559392416.png)

We want the area between the curve $x=\frac{3}{8}{y}^{2}-6$ and the $y$-axis from $y=-4$ to $y=4.$
To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-4}^{4}(\frac{3}{8}{y}^{2}-6)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{\int }_{-4}^{4}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y-6{\int }_{-4}^{4}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{y}^{3}\,{|}_{-4}^{4}-6y\,{|}_{-4}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(64-(-64))-6(4-(-4)) \\  & =16-48 \\  & =-32\end{aligned}
$$

We obtained a negative number because the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis. So, the area that we want is $|-32|=32.$
